claims.summary: Over any characteristic-two field, for m,n>=2 and F_ij=(AB)_ij+delta_ij, no linear functional through degree four both normalizes one, annihilates q F_ij for deg q<=2, and is invariant under every permutation of the inner indices. The two-by-two minor has functional value one from the equations but zero from its even ordered-pair orbits. No Boolean axioms are needed. The added symmetry is impossible even in the satisfiable m=2<=n control, not a degree-four refutation of the rank contradiction.
claims.assessment: Working exact minor and orbit-count control, passed by the sole staged medium reviewer. Symmetry is an added premise; no Boolean axioms or rank-deficiency hypothesis is needed.
claims.rationale: Rules out full symmetric normalized moments as a free simplification of the rank route, while preserving nonsymmetric and partial-symmetry alternatives.
claims.next_action: Retain the obstruction when using invariant theory; do not impose symmetric moments on arbitrary valid designs.

claims.summary: For a finite odd-order group permuting old variables and the full generator/placeholder tuple compatibly over F2, summing all transforms of a Hilbert-like certificate gives an invariant certificate. Size O(|G|(S+1)), depth at most d+1, coefficient degree does not increase. If an input and its placeholder are individually fixed, the axiom-cut normalization commutes with averaging. No full even-order symmetry or lower bound follows.
claims.assessment: Working certificate instance of standard Reynolds averaging with explicit orbit cost, passed by the sole staged medium reviewer. Degree is an upper bound, not an equality; unit-generator and even-order controls included.
claims.rationale: A costed positive control distinguishes valid small odd-group certificate averaging from the false symmetric-functional requirement.
claims.next_action: Use only with the actual group action and orbit cost; it does not prevent the already available invariant axiom cut.

claims.summary: Over a polynomial ring R over any field, if F dot c=1 for F in R^r, then ker(F:R^r->R) is free of rank r-1 and all coefficient certificates form c+ker F. The row splits, making its kernel finitely generated projective; Quillen-Suslin supplies freeness. No effective basis or circuit-size bound is asserted.
claims.assessment: Working elementary split-row consequence of the published Quillen-Suslin theorem, passed by the sole staged medium reviewer; source theorem read in Dicks Theorem6. This is the full polynomial-ring module, not a truncated PC kernel.
claims.rationale: Excludes abstract module nonfreeness as an obstruction distinguishing hard Hilbert-like certificates; filtration and representation cost remain necessary data for that approach.
claims.next_action: Keep any module-complexity proposal costed rather than using abstract freeness as a lower-bound criterion.

claims.summary: For L ordered factors a_i+omega b_i in the central noncommutative extension F4<X>, omega^2=omega+1, with supplied binary-coordinate formulas of size<=B and depth<=e, both coordinates of the product have noncommutative F2 formulas of size O((B+1)L^2) and depth<=e+2ceil(log2 L)+1. Use the regular 2-by-2 matrix representation and balanced ordered products. Empty product handled separately. No free extraction from arbitrary F4 circuits or constant-depth descent claimed.
claims.assessment: Working explicit regular-representation and four-branch balanced formula recurrence, verified by the author and passed by the same reviewer's follow-up. Only supplied factor coordinates are used; no global certificate or fixed-depth descent is proved.
claims.rationale: Pays the local binary coordinate cost for the next complete noncommutative-certificate test without assuming that circuit sharing or constant depth survives.
claims.next_action: Use this local product ledger in the full generator/commutator certificate construction; the global construction remains open.

claims.summary: Li-Tzameret-Wang Theorem1.4: noncommutative IPS formulas over Q or a prime field polynomially simulate ordinary Frege with the source's tautology translation. Boolean and commutator axioms are retained. No fixed-depth guarantee or newly audited modular-presentation transfer is asserted.
claims.assessment: Published source statement; exact definition, theorem and Section3.1 simulation proof including commutator certificates read. Import scope passed by the sole staged medium reviewer; no formula lower bound or new modular-presentation transfer supplied.
claims.rationale: Offers a formula-complexity formulation with established lower-bound methods, but its broader certificate class must first be tested on the selected family.
claims.next_action: Attempt the full binary noncommutative formula certificate for the bounded-degree ternary Tseitin family before attempting a lower bound in this larger class.
